Calculate Perceived Terrain Realism Metric (PTRM)

Source: R/analysis.R
geomorphon_ptrm.Rd

Calculates the Perceived Terrain Realism Metric based on the distribution of geomorphon landform features. The PTRM provides a quantitative estimate of human-perceived terrain realism by relating the proportions of terrain features to their perceived realism.

Usage

geomorphon_ptrm(
  x,
  mode = c("dem", "class"),
  search = 3,
  skip = 0,
  flat_angle_deg = 1,
  dist = 0,
  forms = "forms10",
  coefficients = NULL,
  intercept = -38.02,
  normalizer = 69.96,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

SpatRaster. Either a Digital Elevation Model (when mode = "dem") or a geomorphon classification raster (when mode = "class").

mode

Character. One of "dem" or "class". When "dem", geomorphons are calculated from the input DEM. When "class", the input is assumed to be a pre-computed geomorphon classification. Default: "dem".

search

Numeric. Search radius for geomorphon calculation (only used when mode = "dem"). Units depend on the CRS of the input. Default: 3. This is a convenience default, not a value calibrated against the PTRM paper, so it should not be read as a validated choice.

skip

Numeric. Skip radius for geomorphon calculation (only used when mode = "dem"). Default: 0.

flat_angle_deg

Numeric. Flatness angle threshold in degrees (only used when mode = "dem"). Default: 1.0.

dist

Numeric. Flatness distance (only used when mode = "dem"). Default: 0.

forms

Character. Form system to use: "forms10", "forms6", "forms5", or "forms4". Default: "forms10".

coefficients

Named numeric vector. Custom PTRM coefficients for each geomorphon class. If NULL, uses default values from Rajasekaran et al. (2022). Names should match geomorphon form names. A ten-form vector is reduced to the requested forms system. Default: NULL.

intercept

Numeric. PTRM intercept. Default: -38.02.

normalizer

Numeric. PTRM divisor. Must be finite and non-zero. Default: 69.96.

...

Additional arguments passed to geomorphons() when mode = "dem". Ignored when mode = "class".

Value

A list containing:

ptrm_score

Numeric. PTRM value obtained by dividing the raw score by the normalizer. Scores are raw and may fall outside [0, 1]; higher values indicate more realistic terrain.

raw_score

Numeric. Unnormalized score before division.

proportions

Named numeric vector. Proportion of each observed geomorphon form in the input, named with the canonical system labels.

n_cells

Integer. Total number of valid (non-NA) cells analyzed.

Distance Calculation and Coordinate Reference Systems

The geomorphon classification algorithm assumes planar distances, so it is strongly recommended that elevation data be in a projected coordinate system.

Tiled Processing

When mode = "dem", geomorphons are calculated internally. For large DEMs, this may trigger the automatic tiled processing workflow. See geomorphons() for details.

The PTRM is calculated using the formula:

$$PTRM = \frac{c_0 + \sum_{i=1}^{n} c_i \times p_i}{D}$$

where \(c_0\) is the intercept (-38.02 by default), \(c_i\) are the coefficients for each geomorphon form, \(p_i\) are the proportions of each form in the terrain, and \(D\) is the divisor (69.96 by default). The intercept, normalizer, and coefficients can all be overridden.

The returned score is not clamped or rescaled, so it may fall outside [0, 1] depending on the input distribution and the model parameters. Higher PTRM scores indicate more realistic terrain from a human perception perspective. Rajasekaran et al. (2022) found that real terrain from Arizona achieved a PTRM of 0.76, ranking in the 78th percentile for perceived realism.

References

Rajasekaran, S.D., Kang, H., Čadík, M., Galin, E., Guérin, E., Peytavie, A., Slavík, P., & Mech, R. (2022). PTRM: Perceived Terrain Realism Metric. ACM Transactions on Applied Perception, 19(2), Article 5. doi:10.1145/3514244

Jasiewicz, J., Stepinski, T. (2013). Geomorphons - a pattern recognition approach to classification and mapping of landforms. Geomorphology, 182, 147-156. doi:10.1016/j.geomorph.2012.11.005

See also

geomorphons(), geomorphon_categories()

Examples

library(terra)
library(rgeomorphon)

# Load example DEM
data("volcano", package = "datasets")
dem <- rast(volcano)
crs(dem) <- crs("EPSG:2193")
ext(dem) <- c(1756968, 1757578, 5917000, 5917870)

# Calculate PTRM from DEM
ptrm1 <- geomorphon_ptrm(dem, mode = "dem", search = 7)
print(ptrm1$ptrm_score)
#> [1] -0.2654868

# Or calculate geomorphons first, then PTRM
geo <- geomorphons(dem, search = 7, simplify = TRUE)
ptrm2 <- geomorphon_ptrm(geo, mode = "class")

# Results should be identical
all.equal(ptrm1$ptrm_score, ptrm2$ptrm_score)
#> [1] TRUE
